slides.title: Same Method, Different Task: What the Bitter Lesson Does Not License in Social Simulation
slides.tldr: Bitter lesson limits in social simulation
slides.highlight: This paper argues that scaling LLMs for social simulation fails to replicate the 'bitter lesson' because prediction lacks the stakes inherent in human cooperation, a distinction critical for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLM social simulations fail because prediction lacks stakes, unlike the same-task scaling of the Bitter Lesson.
card.key_idea: Substituting next-token prediction for agent-based modeling violates the Bitter Lesson's same-task condition; predictors lack the interests required for genuine social phenomena.
card.evaluation: 540-agent pilot in common-pool resource games tested persistent consequences; results showed behavioral shifts but no human-like heterogeneity or free-riding.
card.limitation: The pilot environment lacked genuine payoff externalities, preventing a definitive test of whether stakes alone generate interested-party behavior.

slides.title: Scientific Liquidity Agents: An Agent-Based Model of Knowledge Arbitrage in Scientific Communities
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODEL FOR SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ARBITRAGE
slides.highlight: This paper introduces an agent-based model simulating knowledge arbitrage and transfer within scientific communities, offering insights into meso-scale dynamics of information flow and community structure that align with MIMIC's focus on multi-scale societal modeling.

card.one_liner: Agent-based model simulates knowledge arbitrage, revealing verification bottlenecks despite high publication rates.
card.key_idea: Simulates specialists and arbitrageurs using BDI architecture, prerequisite graphs, and LLM/equation policies to model knowledge circulation.
card.evaluation: Two exploratory simulations (10/18 agents) analyzed via publication counts, network connectivity, and replication success rates.
card.limitation: Highly stylized synthetic environment with small agent counts; lacks empirical calibration and realistic artifact content.

slides.title: Just Between Us? Exploring a Wearable-Mediated Channel for Discreet Human-Agent Interaction in a Shared Game Setting
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using in-ear audio and head tilts for discreet human-agent interaction in shared settings, offering insights into awareness and fairness that are relevant to designing embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: Wearable-mediated discreet interaction enables private human-agent communication in shared games without increasing wearer stress.
card.key_idea: Combines in-ear audio cues with head-tilt detection via eSense wearables to facilitate bidirectional, discreet information exchange between a human and a social robot.
card.evaluation: Wizard-of-Oz study with 40 participants in a card game; 39/40 turns protocol-consistent; low stress and high usability reported by wearers.
card.limitation: Wizard-of-Oz setup limits autonomy assessment; non-wearers' varying awareness raises fairness and social acceptability concerns in real deployments.

slides.title: Zero-Shot Coordination among LLM Agents
slides.highlight: This study reveals that frontier LLM agents struggle with zero-shot coordination due to weak reasoning about partner beliefs, directly informing the need for the theory of mind and meta-cognitive capabilities central to ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: Frontier LLM agents fail zero-shot coordination due to weak theory of mind and arbitrary semantic biases.
card.key_idea: Introduces Coordination-friendly definitions (CFDs), shared natural language rules guiding agents to avoid arbitrary conventions and improve coordination.
card.evaluation: Tested on nine simplified Dec-POMDPs (e.g., Cat & Dog, Tiny Hanabi) using frontier LLMs as text and code agents in self-play and cross-play settings.
card.limitation: CFDs may be too restrictive, preventing agents from forming necessary ad-hoc conventions in environments requiring dynamic coordination.

slides.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
slides.tldr: AXIOMATIC RL FOR OPEN MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: This work establishes a principled foundation for learning in open multi-agent systems where only a subset of agents are controllable, directly addressing the challenge of adapting AI teammates to unknown partners in ad-hoc teams.

card.one_liner: Derives value functions from Shapley axioms to improve RL in open multi-agent systems with uncontrolled agents.
card.key_idea: Treats Shapley axioms as structural constraints to derive individual value functions, yielding Shapley and Banzhaf machine templates for NAHT.
card.evaluation: Tested on modified MPE and SMAC benchmarks against IPPO/POAM baselines, showing improved efficiency and generalization to unseen agents.
card.limitation: The Efficiency axiom may reduce generalization to unseen agent types, and computational costs scale with the number of coalitions.

slides.title: A Study on the Effects of Finger Movements on a Humanoid Hugging Robot
slides.highlight: This study examines how finger movement patterns in hugging robots influence user sensations, finding that repetitive and asynchronous movements enhance specific feelings while simultaneous movements evoke care.

card.one_liner: Finger movement patterns in hugging robots significantly influence users' psychological perceptions of care and intent.
card.key_idea: Developed a semi-humanoid robot with independently driven fingers to test how movement patterns (simultaneous vs. asynchronous) affect user emotions.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects experiments with 20 participants using 7-point Likert scales; analyzed via t-tests and ANOVA, showing significant effects on perceived care.
card.limitation: Small sample size (n=20), short duration, and lack of long-term interaction data limit generalizability to real-world healthcare settings.

slides.title: Xinhua Launches Bionic Humanoid News Anchors
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid news anchors highlights advancements in embodied AI and human-robot interaction, relevant to RwB's focus on social robots.

slides.title: Realbotix unveils $11,950 armless tabletop humanoid torsos
slides.highlight: Realbotix has introduced armless tabletop humanoid torsos priced at $11,950, offering a compact form factor for embodied social interaction.

slides.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees
slides.highlight: This work introduces a selective, risk-controlled framework for forecasting emotional departures in conversation using conformal guarantees, offering a robust method for modeling dynamic affective states relevant to social perception.

card.one_liner: Emotion value forecasting fails against persistence baselines, but predicting departure occurrence with conformal risk guarantees is viable.
card.key_idea: Shifts target from predicting emotional values to detecting departures from persistence, using selective commitment policies and dialogue-level conformal risk control.
card.evaluation: Tested on IEMOCAP, MELD, DailyDialog, EmoryNLP using CCC, AUPRC, LT-F1; validated via 5-fold CV, leakage tests, and empirical risk bounds.
card.limitation: Persistence barrier relies on oracle historical state access; risk guarantees incur high abstention rates, reducing recall significantly.

slides.title: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR HUMAN PERCEPTION OF VOICE IDENTITY
slides.highlight: VIPBench evaluates how human listeners perceive voice identity across real, cloned, and morphed recordings, revealing significant divergences between speaker-recognition models and human judgments. This is relevant to HyECHO as it provides a framework for assessing the reliability of identity recognition and diarization in hybrid human-AI teams where synthetic voices may be present.

card.one_liner: VIPBench evaluates voice identity models against human perception, revealing significant divergence from metadata labels.
card.key_idea: Benchmark using 124k human judgments on real, cloned, and morphed voices to align speaker representations with perceptual identity.
card.evaluation: Tested 11 models on 4 tasks; supervised models align best (61% variance explained), while clones often perceived as different speakers.
card.limitation: Models trained on metadata labels fail to capture perceptual identity, especially for voice clones, requiring direct human-judgment training.

slides.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
slides.highlight: This paper presents an open smart-ring platform that integrates physiological and motion sensing to enable human-centric robot interaction, offering insights relevant to RwB's work on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

card.one_liner: OpenZilo is an open smart-ring platform enabling human-centric robot interaction via speech, gestures, and physiological sensing.
card.key_idea: Integrates microphone, IMU, PPG, and temperature sensors with modular software separating acquisition, event interpretation, policy, and robot execution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 10 participants on speech/gesture control (90.4%/88.8% success) and simulated physiological triggers; descriptive metrics only.
card.limitation: Small convenience sample, simulated physiological events, and lack of statistical significance tests limit generalizability and real-world validity.

slides.title: Consolidating Reasoning with Test-Time Training
slides.tldr: TEST-TIME TRAINING FOR MULTI-AGENT REASONING CONSOLIDATION
slides.highlight: This paper introduces TTT-Consolidate, a framework that uses test-time training to consolidate multi-agent reasoning trajectories into parametric representations, enabling more effective solution synthesis than standard voting or context aggregation. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of developing AI teammates that adapt at test time and improve reasoning through meta-cognitive self-correction.

card.one_liner: TTT-Consolidate uses test-time training to consolidate multi-agent reasoning trajectories into a LoRA adapter for improved solution synthesis.
card.key_idea: Meta-learned bi-level optimization where an inner loop encodes reasoning trajectories into a LoRA adapter via gradient updates, and an outer loop synthesizes the final answer.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on math/STEM benchmarks using OpenParallelThinking; outperforms baselines by up to 20% and recovers from incorrect trajectories, validated with compute-matched controls.
card.limitation: Requires constructing a new 13K-problem dataset and incurs additional test-time compute for gradient-based adaptation, though gains persist under matched budgets.

slides.title: Precision Through Play: Enhancing Fundamental Laparoscopic Skill Acquisition Via Gamified XR and Pseudo-Haptics
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how gamified XR with pseudo-haptic feedback can enhance precision in instrument handling, offering a scalable model for skill acquisition relevant to MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill estimation and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: Gamified XR with pseudo-haptics enhances laparoscopic instrument alignment and skill acquisition.
card.key_idea: Interactive XR platform uses gamification and pseudo-haptic feedback to monitor and correct instrument angular deviation during practice.
card.evaluation: Preliminary evaluations indicate improved precision and reduced angular variance, but specific datasets, baselines, and metrics are not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Relies on preliminary results without detailed quantitative benchmarks or comparisons against established training methods.

slides.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that users can effectively interpret underspecified alerts from AI systems by leveraging prior knowledge, a capability relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling human-AI team state and engagement.

card.one_liner: Pragmatic AI assistants that omit known details improve detection speed and accuracy in time-critical monitoring tasks.
card.key_idea: An RSA-based planner adapts alert specificity to user prior knowledge, saving time to cover more critical events than fully specified baselines.
card.evaluation: Preregistered study (N=114) in DroneWorld; compared pragmatic planner vs. baseline on detection, latency, and belief accuracy using mixed-effects models.
card.limitation: Benefit concentrated in low-awareness scenes; users may distrust or ignore underspecified alerts if they suspect system incompetence rather than cooperation.

slides.title: LumiTac: Compact, High-Rate Six-Axis Optical Tactile Sensing for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work introduces LumiTac, a compact, low-cost optical tactile sensor capable of high-rate six-axis force and moment reconstruction, validated for tactile-guided manipulation and physical human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: LumiTac is a compact, low-cost optical tactile sensor enabling high-rate six-axis force and moment measurement for robotics.
card.key_idea: Uses spatially distributed RGBW emitters/receivers across silicone layers; an MLP reconstructs six-axis loads from 20 optical channels.
card.evaluation: Validated via reference F/T sensor (R²>0.96, MAE<0.2N); demonstrated 303Hz update rate in combined loading and robot control tasks.
card.limitation: Accuracy relies on silicone stability and optical alignment; ambient light and elastomer nonlinearity remain calibration challenges.

slides.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces a meta-control policy for LLM agents that learns to dynamically route between different memory utilization strategies during test-time adaptation, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of agents that adapt beyond in-context learning and self-monitor their cognitive processes.

card.one_liner: OMCE uses a contextual bandit to dynamically route experience usage and consolidation in LLM agents.
card.key_idea: A lightweight meta-controller selects among four cognitive actions (DIRECT, EPISODE, GUIDE, DISTILL) using retrieval signals and online bandit updates.
card.evaluation: Tested on four benchmarks with four LLMs; OMCE improved first-attempt success by up to 20.5 points and reduced token use 5.7–62.5x vs ACE.
card.limitation: Relies on timely feedback; sparse rewards or distribution shifts can degrade performance, and memory growth may cause retrieval redundancy.

slides.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
slides.highlight: This work explores haptic shared control strategies for multi-robot systems, providing operators with tactile feedback on system connectivity and enabling adaptive supervision at varying scales, which aligns with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation and intent alignment.

card.one_liner: Haptic shared control for multi-robot systems using decentralized connectivity maintenance with realistic sensor constraints.
card.key_idea: Extends decentralized connectivity maintenance to handle limited field-of-view and body-frame measurements, enabling haptic feedback for variable-scale group control.
card.evaluation: Validated via realistic simulations and a user study with 20 participants, comparing three control methods with and without haptic feedback.
card.limitation: Relies on simulation fidelity; real-world deployment requires addressing dynamic model limitations like quadrotor tilt affecting field-of-view.

slides.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework using mechanistic interpretability to enforce counterfactual fairness in transformers via activation steering, offering a task-agnostic method to mitigate bias in decision-making systems.

card.one_liner: MICF uses mechanistic interpretability to steer transformer activations for counterfactual fairness.
card.key_idea: Reformulates counterfactual fairness via activation patching to identify causal bias pathways, then mitigates them through inference-time activation steering.
card.evaluation: Tested on UTICalc and COMPAS tabular datasets using TabPFN, measuring causal effects and accuracy against flip and LLM-generated counterfactuals.
card.limitation: Relies on LLMs for counterfactual generation, assuming they encode valid causal knowledge, which may introduce residual bias from latent confounding.

slides.title: InteractionBench: Measuring Timing, Task Accuracy, Whisper and Volume, and Grounding in Real-Time Voice Systems
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating real-time voice systems across timing, task accuracy, volume control, and grounding, providing metrics relevant to assessing the conversational dynamics of AI agents in HyECHO's hybrid team contexts.

card.one_liner: InteractionBench evaluates real-time voice systems across timing, task accuracy, paralinguistics, and groundedness.
card.key_idea: A unified harness measures four dimensions on identical recorded audio, using rule-based scoring for timing and LLM judges for semantics.
card.evaluation: Tested seven systems (hosted, open, cascade) on 221 items; hosted models outperformed open models in groundedness and task accuracy.
card.limitation: Timing scores for hosted systems include network latency, and protocol inconsistencies (e.g., interruption timing) hinder direct comparisons.

slides.title: Holistic Parallel Supervision for Expressive Speech to Speech Translation
slides.tldr: Holistic Parallel Supervision for Expressive S2ST
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-data strategy combining professional dubbing and voice conversion to align content, prosody, timing, and speaker identity in speech-to-speech translation. It is relevant to HyECHO as it addresses the preservation of expressive and paralinguistic cues, which are critical for modeling engagement and group norms in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: Combining professional dubbing with voice conversion creates holistic parallel data, significantly improving expressive speech-to-speech translation.
card.key_idea: Constructs training pairs by aligning dubbing content/prosody/timing and applying voice conversion to match speaker identity, enabling direct end-to-end expressive modeling.
card.evaluation: Tested on En-De/En-Es using mExpresso; metrics include BLEU, prosody, timing, speaker similarity, and human expressiveness ratings against CVSS-T baselines.
card.limitation: Depends on availability of high-quality professional dubbing data and accurate voice conversion, which may introduce artifacts or fail in low-resource languages.

slides.title: Eyedaptic launches Eva, an agentic AI visual assistant for patients with retinal disease
slides.highlight: The launch of an agentic AI visual assistant demonstrates the application of autonomous agents in specialized healthcare contexts, relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates.

slides.title: Tairex Launches Multi-Agent AI System to Transform Clinical Collaboration and Decision Support
slides.highlight: Tairex has launched a multi-agent AI system designed to enhance clinical collaboration and decision support, offering a relevant case study for MIMIC's exploration of agent-based models in complex societal systems.
